posts.post: If you could ask Queen Elizabeth II one thing, what would it be?

Sudden bladder emptying
33, male, 6'3, 225#, Caucasian, smoker, ASD, depression, Wellbutrin  About a month ago I was about 200 miles away from home and getting ready to drive home. I urinated before leaving, about 15 miles into the drive I stopped at a rest area and urinated again. I drove approximately 60-70 more miles and my bladder suddenly let go. I knew I needed to urinate but had no where to stop so was waiting for the next town. Some days I seem to urinate very frequently other days I may only pee three times the whole day. My question is since kinda embarrassing should I tell primary, or is it likely just a one off thing? I have appointment with primary Thursday morning.

Painful mole
I have a mole on the upper part of my back. For the past year or so I periodically get a sharp pain that I would describe as either it being cut by a razor, or being burnt. It is isolated to the mole. I am not able to get a clear picture of the mole. It is symmetrical, and a even medium brown in color. I did get a nasty sunburn across the upper back/shoulders about two years ago. Is there any reason to be overly concerned about the mole? It does not look like a pimple is developing by it.

Resume help
Can someone help me reword this paragraph i have in the skills section of my resume?  &#x200B;   At any public facing role I have had, I have proven to exhibit and am always striving to use my business experience and knowledge to provide superior customer service. My greatest strengths include collaboration, being team player and remaining positive. My particular hard skills involve math and working with numbers, along with organizing information.

Want to skip appointment with PsyD
So last April I went into a neuropsychologist (doctorate in 2015) and had an evaluation for autism. The doctor came to the conclusion that it was ASD and not ADHD and was adamant that there was not ADHD. Fast forward a few months and I am talking to a psychiatrist (doctorate in 1976) about an off label treatment for depression. He tells me that my idea wont work, but tells me that his pretty confident that ADHD is there. He doesnt comment on ASD one way or the other. He prescribes Strattera and tells me to talk to primary about stimulants. I forward the message from the psychiatrist to primary. He immediately puts in a referral to a PsyD to get a full ADHD evaluation. I went to the appointments, and did everything i needed to. I am 95% he will tell me ADHD inattentive. I don't think he will comment on ASD since he is not an evaluator for that. Long story short, tomorrow I am supposed to go in and have the results session. I have been dreading this appointment since before I made it. I will go, but i am at the point i wish i never started asking "Why am I the way I am".      My username will continue to fit permanently i guess.

Looking for a PsyD opinion
Male, 33, 6'3", 225#, Caucasian, smoker, depression,  Bupropion 450mg/daily  This year at work I elected to get the no deductible copay only insurance plan so I could try to stabilize/understand my mental health.   In April I saw a neuropsychologist that evaluated and said ASD no ADHD.   In August I saw a psychiatrist who said ADHD, and didn't comment on ASD.  PCP put in a referral for a full ADHD evaluation. This PsyD says he doesn't think ASD but didn't test for that specifically. He doesn't think ADHD because I scored in the 93rd percentile in the 'harder' executive function tests, and scored in the very deficient in the 'easier' ones. He thinks all my issue is depression clouding my mind on simple tasks, and when doing something complicated my brain pushes the depression thoughts out. He also said there could be moderate borderline personality disorder.  So now I have had three professionals say three distinctively different things and feel like the last year has been a waste of time, money, and energy.   My question is why is there so much variation between them? I get that psychology testing is subjective to an extent but shouldn't they be at least in the same ballpark?

Suicide is inevitable
For the past twenty years I have had a deep depression rooted in being gay. I am conservatively Christian and hold a traditional sex ethic. I have being trying to reconcile those two things with no success for seemingly ever. The depression got worse and I realized that one day I would ultimately end up committing suicide eventually. This past year I have been trying to work on my mental health and 'get help' as all the mental health marketing says to do. It has been an absolute joke. Trying to get help when you are not in immediate crisis, or an addict/junky is almost impossible. I have been treated like I am seeking drugs, like I am seeking disability, or just malingering to malinger. I have decided to quit going to the doctor at all and go back to white knuckling my depression until it is time for it to end.

The serenity of it all
I have been dealing with mostly untreated depression my whole life. This past year I went and tried to get help and have gotten no where. I have now come to the conclusion that I just need to accept that the depression is permanent and won't be leaving. With that I have decided that one day (not today or tomorrow but one day) I will end up getting away from the depression by forcing myself to leave this world. The serenity of accepting this has brought so much more peace.

Antidepressant question
33, Male, Caucasian, Smoker, 6'3", 230#, Depression, Anxiety  For the past six months I have been working with primary on depression and other mental health issues. He started me on Prozac which I took for a month but didn't like because of ED type side effects. Primary switched me to Wellbutrin and over the summer that seemed to work well at first. As September and October came my depression nosedived. Partially because of external issues going. Today I met with the primary and have not been taking Wellbutrin for past week. My depression is to deeply rooted to really think it will ever disappear. He gave me a couple of options to consider. First was increase Wellbutrin from 300mg a day to 450. The second was Paxil, the third was Effexor XR. I am hesitant as to go with the Paxil or Effexor since from what I understand they have the same ED side effect as Prozac. The higher dose Wellbutrin I would possibly consider. Right now I am leaning towards St John's Wort, fish oil and the lamp rather than any Rx. Are there other medications I should ask doctor about? Are the 'natural' options effective against major depression?
